title: Toasted Sesame and Spring Onion Waffles
changes_from_base: A savoury buttermilk batter with sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, black pepper, grated cheese and spring onions, with whites whisked to medium peaks; served with an egg if you like.
summary: Savoury sesame waffles studded with spring onion and cheese, crisp enough to top with a poached or fried egg.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
Parmesan, pecorino or white Cheddar, grated
spring onions, thinly sliced (or 8 g chopped chives)
large eggs, at room temperature, separated
unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the iron
poached or fried eggs, to serve (optional)

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 231 g plain flour, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 1¼ tsp baking powder, ¼ tsp bicarbonate of soda, ⅜ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper together, stir in 100 g grated cheese and 4 sliced spring onions, and make a well in the centre.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: Put 2 egg whites in one bowl, then drop the 2 egg yolks into the well with 300 ml buttermilk and 1 tsp sesame oil and stir gently into a batter without overmixing.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites to medium peaks and fold them in gently until just combined, then fold in 60 g melted butter.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and brush lightly with butter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour a heaped 160 ml batter per waffle and cook until golden and crisp, buttering the iron between batches.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve as they're ready, or keep warm in a 93 °C oven, topped with a poached or fried egg if you like.

tips: Stir the cheese and spring onion into the dry ingredients before adding any liquid, so they're evenly spread through the batter.
Fold the whisked egg whites in gently so the finished waffle stays light rather than dense.
Brush the iron lightly with butter between batches as needed so each waffle releases cleanly.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the iron. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
